Select a sparse set of sample pairs for model fitting

Source: R/sparse_fit.R
sparse_diss.Rd

Selects a subset of sample pairs to be used for fitting rrGDM, such that every sample is in exactly the same number of pairs (knn + n_random). Each sample is paired with its knn nearest neighbours, which inform its local position, and with n_random random samples, which ensure that the global structure (including distant samples) is represented. Selection is based on the observed dissimilarities only.

Usage

sparse_diss(
  Y,
  knn = 10,
  n_random = 3,
  max_zeros = Inf,
  dist_method = "bray",
  trans = function(x) x,
  binary = FALSE,
  k_pcoa = 2,
  link = "identity",
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

Y

A community matrix or data frame (samples x species), or an object of class dist. If a dist object is supplied, dist_method, trans and binary are ignored.

knn

Integer. Number of nearest neighbours per sample. Default is 10.

n_random

Integer. Number of random pairs per sample. Default is 3.

max_zeros

Integer or Inf. Maximum number of pairs with a dissimilarity of exactly 0 per sample. Default is Inf.

dist_method

Dissimilarity index: a method of vegdist (e.g. 'bray', 'jaccard', 'euclidean'); 'sorensen' is Bray-Curtis on presence-absence data. Ignored if Y is a dist object. Default is 'bray'.

trans

Transformation applied to Y before calculating dissimilarities. Default is no transformation.

binary

Logical indicating whether Y should be converted to presence-absence before calculating dissimilarities. Default is FALSE.

k_pcoa

Integer (at least 2) or NULL. Number of PCoA axes of the full dissimilarity matrix stored for 2D representation. Use NULL to skip it. Default is 2.

link

Character string: 'identity' (default), 'negexp' or 'neggaus'. Link function of the model to be fitted (see rrGDM). The PCoA is computed on dissimilarities transformed to the scale of latent distances (e.g. -log(1 - diss) for 'negexp'), after setting dissimilarities above 0.99 to 0.99. This does not affect which pairs are selected.

seed

An integer passed to set.seed() at the start, so it changes the state of R's random number generator. Default is NULL (no seed is set).

Value

An object of class sparse_diss: a list including edges, a two-column integer matrix (s1, s2) of the pairs kept, which rrGDM uses to subset the dissimilarities (argument sparse), and pairs, a data frame with the pairs, their dissimilarity (diss) and their type ('knn', 'random' or 'zero'). Each pair is stored once, with s1 < s2. degree gives the number of pairs per sample. The other components are the sample names (id), the number of samples and pairs (n_samples, n_pairs_full, n_pairs, n_zero_pairs), the settings used (knn, n_random, n_per_sample, max_zeros, link, dist_method, binary), the number of connected groups of samples (n_components), the PCoA used by plot.sparse_diss (pcoa, NULL if k_pcoa = NULL) and the matched call (call).

Details

Pairs are sorted by dissimilarity and kept if both samples have fewer than knn pairs (and fewer than max_zeros for zero dissimilarities). The remaining pairs up to knn + n_random, are filled with random pairs among samples with free slots. Because the number of pairs per sample is fixed, a sample may be paired with a sample that is not among its own knn nearest neighbours. Pairs with a dissimilarity of exactly 0 (identical samples) are only added in the nearest-neighbour step, never in the random step.

One sample has one pair fewer if both the number of samples and knn + n_random are odd. A warning is given if some samples fall short or if the pairs do not connect all samples (increase n_random).

See also

plot.sparse_diss, print.sparse_diss
